claim: A B.Tech-level LTspice active-filter design exercise for a biomedical EKG amplifier chain specifies exact component values for a first-order low-pass filter: Rf=100kOhm, Cf=10nF, Rs=20kOhm, LT1490 op-amp, +/-10V rails, RL=1kOhm.
stance_target: reproducible LTspice project spec for EKG signal-conditioning filter
scope_conditions: Northeastern EECE 2510 biomedical circuits lab, LTspice simulation
quoted_support: Use Rf=100kΩ ,Cf=10nF ,∧Rs=20kΩ. Use +− 10V DC power supplies for the op-amp

claim: The lab specifies an AC sweep simulation directive '.ac dec 100 1 1000000' to characterize filter cutoff frequency from 1Hz to 1MHz at 100 points per decade.
stance_target: standard LTspice AC-analysis procedure for filter characterization

claim: A companion active high-pass filter for the same EKG chain uses Rs=100kOhm, Cs=10nF, Rf=200kOhm and is analyzed for in-band gain and cutoff frequency over the same 1Hz-1MHz sweep.
stance_target: reproducible LTspice project spec for EKG high-pass stage
quoted_support: change your circuit so that it is an active high pass filter shown in Figure 3 with RS=100kΩ ,CS = 10nF ,Rf=200kΩ

claim: A 200Hz, 0.5Vpp square-wave pulse source is used in transient analysis to observe filter distortion of a square wave, with FFT used to view frequency-domain content up to 5kHz.
stance_target: time-domain/FFT validation method for active filter projects
quoted_support: use a pulsed source to produce a 200 Hz square wave with 0.5V p-p ... displaying the FFT up to 5 kHz is about right.
